science.scope: Independent regression assessment of the repaired English within the six original findings, without reopening source/Chinese/figure approvals.

checks.conclusion: The surface-tension model is positive and limited by competing forces. Gravity and liquid flow remain. The drop is explicitly water, not water in a foreign elastic bag; no solid skin tears. The film comparison remains only a comparison.
Liquid wall, continued straw attachment and an open escape route precede the conditional shrinking explanation. A sealed bubble is not promised to shrink by this route.

The upward part of surface pull, buoyancy and wetting are all retained and explained. Careful placement is not a guarantee. Water striders are identified as insects; their support is not explained as ice or solid water.

Spreading/sticking, hole size, pressure and temporary retention remain conditional, with possible leakage explicitly stated. The pressure sentence's ambiguous subject is a readability/referent finding, not a demonstrated new unqualified physical law. Ink, soap, fabric and plant effects are not attributed to surface tension alone.

Ball shape remains conditional on weak competing deformation and contact. Smaller drops are compared in the same liquid/similar surroundings. Air resistance and larger-drop deformation remain. Refraction, internal reflection and dispersion are separately glossed. Gravity remains present in microgravity, and wall contact/disturbance can change shape.

Molecules remain moving and non-intentional, with no universal inward force or permanent inward migration. Stable temperature/composition/neighboring material and weak competing forces condition the area/energy argument. The rubber comparison stays limited. Equal edge lengths and coefficient are distinguished from changing total pull; nearly incompressible liquids and density are not declared invariant under all conditions.
No two-phase coexistence, phase-equilibrium, melting, boiling, vapor-pressure or fixed-transition-temperature claim is added by the repaired English.

findings.title: Name water retention as the pressure-dependent effect
evidence: Whether this works depends on the hole size and wetting.
Wetting means how water spreads over and sticks to the mesh.
It also depends on pressure, or how hard the water pushes.
findings.problem: In the actual saved paragraph 28, It immediately follows the definition of wetting. An eight-year-old can reasonably attach It to wetting rather than to the sieve's ability to hold water in paragraph 27. The pressure condition's intended subject is therefore unclear even though the relevant science terms are present.
findings.requiredAction: Replace only this pronoun-led sentence with an explicit retention subject, for example: Whether the sieve holds water also depends on pressure, or how hard the water pushes. Update the corresponding saved flow paragraph from the changed draft. Keep the neighboring wetting definition, hole-size qualification and possible leakage unchanged.
findings.acceptance: A child can tell immediately that pressure affects whether the sieve holds water. The repaired draft and flow agree, and the adjacent paragraphs still explain wetting and possible passage. No new science, source/Chinese/figure review or whole-lesson rewrite is needed.
